newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria gives aid to rebel-hit families.
newsitem.headline: Algeria gives aid to rebel-hit families.

text.p: Algerian authorities gave food, clothes and cash on Thursday to 204 families in the eastern province of Tebessa to help them after relatives were killed by Moslem guerrillas, the official Algerian news agency APS said.
Tebessa, in eastern Algeria near the border with Tunisia, is seen as an area of relatively low violence in the conflict in which about 60,000 people have died since early 1992.
"This token aid underscores the state's great interest and attention for families who have been victims of criminality," said an unnamed local government official.

The aid, also given by local authorities elsewhere, is to help families during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, expected to start on Friday or Saturday in Algeria depending on the sighting of the moon.
Algeria's government has set up a fund to pay monthly allowances to bereaved families, equivalent to at least the salaries of its members killed by Moslem guerrillas.
